about.intro_content: Prof. Ming Song is a Professor in the Department of Head and Neck Surgery at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou. He was recognised as a Distinguished Young Doctor at SYSUCC in 2008.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Song's research examines head and neck tumour biology, tumorigenesis and drug resistance, informed by a research visit to MD Anderson Cancer Center, USA (2011–2012). His clinical and research interests include free flap reconstruction after salvage surgery for recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma and biomarkers in tongue squamous cell cancer. He currently serves as Principal Investigator on a trial evaluating surgery with or without neoadjuvant stereotactic body radiotherapy plus chemoimmunotherapy in resectable oral and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Ming Song

items.question: Does Prof. Ming Song accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to head and neck cancer at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Song's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Song specialises in head and neck surgical oncology, including oral and oropharyngeal cancer, and reconstructive free flap surgery.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Song involved in clinical trials for head and neck cancer?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Song is Principal Investigator on a trial evaluating neoadjuvant radiotherapy plus chemoimmunotherapy before surgery for resectable oral and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.

items.question: Does Prof. Song perform reconstructive surgery after head and neck cancer surgery?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Song has published research on free flap reconstruction techniques for repairing head and neck defects, including after salvage surgery for recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
